paragraphs.title: Jeremiah in the Cistern and His Rescue

answers: The princes
The women
The Chaldeans
easy.explanation: Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jucal, and Pashur, who were princes, heard Jeremiah's words.
easy.q: Who heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken unto all the people?

answers: He would be imprisoned
He would live
He would be carried to Egypt
easy.explanation: Jeremiah said that whoever went forth to the Chaldeans would live.
easy.q: What did Jeremiah say would happen to the person who went forth to the Chaldeans?

answers: Into the king's house
Into the gate of Benjamin
Into the dungeon
easy.explanation: The princes cast Jeremiah into the dungeon of Malchiah in the court of the prison.
easy.q: Where did the princes cast Jeremiah?

answers: They thought his words weakened the soldiers and the people
He refused to leave the city
He helped the king of Babylon
medium.explanation: They said that Jeremiah weakened the hands of the men of war and all the people.
medium.q: Why did the princes ask that Jeremiah be put to death?

answers: He strengthens them for battle
He discourages them and weakens their resolve to fight
He heals their wounds
medium.explanation: The princes meant that Jeremiah's words discouraged the soldiers and weakened their determination.
medium.q: What does the expression “he weakeneth the hands of the men of war” mean?

answers: He left the city
He reported only to the princes
He went to the king and asked that Jeremiah be rescued
medium.explanation: Ebed-melech went out of the king's house and spoke to the king about Jeremiah.
medium.q: What did Ebed-melech do after hearing about Jeremiah's condition?

answers: Remaining in the city would bring death, but going forth to the Chaldeans would bring life
The rich would live and the poor would die
The soldiers would live and the princes would die
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah presented surrender to the Chaldeans as the way to live, while remaining in the city would lead to death.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in Jeremiah's words about the inhabitants' fate?

answers: The dungeon was full of water
The rescuers tried to lift him without hurting him
The princes wanted to put him back into the dungeon
challenge.explanation: Ebed-melech placed old cloths and rags under Jeremiah's armholes before lifting him with cords.
challenge.q: What do the cords and old cloths show about Jeremiah's rescue?

answers: He became king
He left the city
He remained in the court of the prison
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah was rescued from the dungeon but remained in the court of the prison.
challenge.q: What was Jeremiah's condition after he was brought out of the dungeon?

answers: King Zedekiah
Ebed-melech
The captains of the army
easy.explanation: King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah and brought him to a private place.
easy.q: Who summoned Jeremiah for a conversation?

answers: Build the city
Give him counsel and hide nothing from him
Go forth to fight
easy.explanation: The king told Jeremiah, “I will ask thee a thing; hide nothing from me.”
easy.q: What did Zedekiah ask Jeremiah to do?

answers: The king and the city would be preserved
The city would immediately burn
The king would remain in the dungeon
easy.explanation: Jeremiah said that Zedekiah's soul would live, his house would live, and the city would not be burned.
easy.q: What did Jeremiah say would happen if Zedekiah went forth unto the king of Babylon's princes?

answers: He did not know the word of the Lord
He feared that the king would put him to death
He wanted to hide it from the people
medium.explanation: Jeremiah feared that Zedekiah might kill him or refuse to listen to his counsel.
medium.q: Why was Jeremiah afraid to tell the king the word of the Lord?

answers: You will not be able to escape from them
You will not be able to speak to them
You will not be able to help them
medium.explanation: The expression means that Zedekiah would not be able to escape from the Chaldeans if he refused.
medium.q: What does the expression “thou shalt not escape out of their hand” mean?

answers: Surrender would preserve the city, while refusal would bring its destruction
Surrender would burn the city, while refusal would save it
The king's decision had no connection with the city's fate
medium.explanation: Jeremiah presented surrender as the way to preserve the city and refusal as the way to bring destruction.
medium.q: What was the connection between surrender and the city's fate?

answers: To remain in the dungeon or move to the temple
To go forth to Babylon's princes and live, or refuse and suffer the city's destruction
To fight the princes or flee to Egypt
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah gave Zedekiah the choice between surrender and life or refusal and destruction.
challenge.q: What choice did Jeremiah set before Zedekiah?

answers: He wanted to conceal the conversation and his promise
He had already surrendered to the king of Babylon
He did not believe Jeremiah at all
challenge.explanation: The oath was made secretly, showing that the king wanted the conversation and his promise kept from others.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the fact that Zedekiah swore secretly to Jeremiah?

answers: The women in the king's house
The princes who wanted to harm Jeremiah
The princes of the king of Babylon
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the officials who had opposed Jeremiah and sought his life.
challenge.q: Who are those described as “these men that seek thy life”?

paragraphs.title: The Vision of the Royal Household and the City's Destruction

answers: It would be rebuilt
It would be burned with fire
It would be given to the people of Judah
easy.explanation: Jeremiah said that the city would be given into the hand of the Chaldeans and burned with fire.
easy.q: What would happen to the city if Zedekiah did not go forth unto the king of Babylon's princes?

answers: The king's wives and children
Only the men of war
Only the princes
easy.explanation: The vision says that Zedekiah's wives and children would be brought forth to the Chaldeans.
easy.q: Who would be brought forth unto the Chaldeans?

answers: He would escape from the city
He would be taken by the king of Babylon
He would remain king in Jerusalem
easy.explanation: Jeremiah said that Zedekiah would be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon.

answers: Zedekiah's refusal to go forth unto the king of Babylon's princes
Ebed-melech's departure
Jeremiah's remaining in the court of the prison
medium.explanation: The vision described what would happen if Zedekiah refused to surrender.
medium.q: What caused the destruction described in the vision?

answers: Your feet have been healed
You are trapped in a difficult situation from which it is hard to escape
You have safely left the city
medium.explanation: The expression pictures helplessness and entrapment caused by following the wrong advisers.
medium.q: What does the expression “thy feet are sunk in the mire” mean in the women's words?

answers: Both would be preserved if the king remained
The royal household would be brought to the Chaldeans and the city would be burned
Only the family would suffer while the city would be preserved
medium.explanation: The vision includes both the removal of the royal household and the burning of Jerusalem.
medium.q: How are the royal family's fate and the city's fate connected?

answers: To show that the king had lost control and had been overcome by his advisers
To prove that the women led the war
To describe the king's daily life in the palace
challenge.explanation: Their words portray the king as having been persuaded and trapped by the men he trusted.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the women speaking to the king in the vision?

answers: The city burns, then the family leaves, and finally the king is captured
The royal household is brought to the Chaldeans, the king is taken, and the city is burned
The king escapes, the city is preserved, and the family returns
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the household being brought out, Zedekiah being taken, and the city being burned.
challenge.q: What order of events is presented in the vision?

answers: Obeying the Lord's counsel brings life, while refusing it brings destruction
The king could choose only to fight
The city would be preserved in every case
challenge.explanation: The vision illustrates the disastrous result of rejecting the Lord's command through Jeremiah.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between Jeremiah's earlier words and this vision emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Conversation Is Concealed and Jeremiah Remains Detained

answers: Tell it to the people
Write it on the city gate
Let no man know about it
easy.explanation: Zedekiah told Jeremiah, “Let no man know of these words.”
easy.q: What did Zedekiah command Jeremiah concerning their conversation?

answers: That he had presented his supplication before the king not to return him to Jonathan's house
That the king had declared war
That he was about to go forth to the Chaldeans
easy.explanation: The king instructed Jeremiah to say that he had asked not to be returned to Jonathan's house to die there.
easy.q: What was Jeremiah to say if the princes asked him about the conversation?

answers: In the king's house
In the court of the prison
At the gate of Benjamin
easy.explanation: Jeremiah abode in the court of the prison until the day that Jerusalem was taken.
easy.q: Where did Jeremiah remain until Jerusalem was taken?

answers: So the princes would not learn what had been discussed
So Jeremiah could escape
So the people could be told of a victory
medium.explanation: The king wanted the contents of his conversation with Jeremiah kept from the princes.
medium.q: Why did Zedekiah want the conversation concealed?

answers: Everyone must know
No person is to know
Only the Chaldeans must know
medium.explanation: The command means that the conversation was to remain secret.
medium.q: What does the expression “Let no man know” mean?

answers: They killed him
They left off speaking with him
They released him from prison
medium.explanation: After hearing Jeremiah's answer, the princes stopped questioning him because the matter was not perceived.
medium.q: How did the princes respond to Jeremiah's answer?

answers: The king wanted to protect the secret conversation and Jeremiah
The king wanted to deliver Jeremiah to the princes
The king had not spoken with Jeremiah at all
challenge.explanation: The instructions concealed the conversation and helped prevent the princes from harming Jeremiah.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from Zedekiah's instructions about answering the princes?

answers: He was released before the siege began
He was rescued from the dungeon but was not set free
He became one of the city's princes
challenge.explanation: Although Jeremiah was brought out of the dungeon, he continued to remain in custody.
challenge.q: What does the fact that Jeremiah remained detained until Jerusalem was taken signify?

answers: Jerusalem was taken, in keeping with the warnings of the city's destruction
Jerusalem was preserved despite Jeremiah's words
The princes ended the siege
challenge.explanation: The chapter ends with Jerusalem being taken, fulfilling the judgment Jeremiah had warned about.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the chapter's ending and Jeremiah's prophecies?
